Lessons learned: (1) All limit changes require 72-hour advance notice. (2) Clients must have a documented escalation path. (3) Rate limit headers should be included in all API responses.
API versioning policy: breaking changes require a deprecation notice period of at least 30 days. Rate limit adjustments are considered breaking changes when they reduce the existing limit.

events.handoff: Retrieved all available project documents; the corpus contains an API validation rule (empty arrays are rejected, JSON Schema validation enforced) and general API-design/postmortem guidance. Using these plus universal best-practice, a full implementation-and-review plan has been produced for the GET /api/glamup 404 fix.

output_document.summary:
The reference corpus surfaces three usable sources: (1) api-design-guidelines.md establishes that all API inputs are validated against a JSON Schema and that empty arrays are rejected — this directly supports returning a 404 (resource not found) rather than propagating an unhandled exception as a 500 when the GlamUp table is empty. (2) postmortem-lessons.md requires that rate-limit headers be included in all API responses and that clients have a documented escalation path — this reminds us to keep the 404 JSON body machine-readable and consistent with existing error envelopes. (3) incident-report-2024-q3.md illustrates the cost of undocumented API behaviour changes and reinforces the need for review before the fix ships. No source file for the route handler itself was found in the corpus, so the implementation plan below follows conventional REST / MVC patterns that are consistent with the guidelines retrieved.

PLAN

1. LOCATE THE HANDLER
   File to edit: the controller/route that serves GET /api/glamup (likely routes/glamup.js, controllers/glamupController.js, or equivalent). The developer must identify the exact file in the working tree.

2. IMPLEMENT THE FIX (small, surgical change)
   Current behaviour: the handler issues a DB query and either throws an unhandled exception or falls through to a generic 500 middleware when the GlamUp table is empty.
   New behaviour:
     a. After the DB query resolves, check whether the result set is empty (e.g. rows.length === 0 or result === null).
     b. If empty, return immediately:
        HTTP 404
        Content-Type: application/json
        Body: { "error": "not_found", "message": "No GlamUp records exist." }
     c. Otherwise continue with the existing 200 success path.
   This is consistent with the project rule that 'empty arrays are rejected' and that all responses carry a structured JSON body.

3. WRITE / UPDATE TESTS
   a. Unit test (mock DB layer):
      - Mock the GlamUp DB query to return an empty result.
      - Assert response status === 404.
      - Assert response body is valid JSON with keys 'error' and 'message'.
   b. Integration / contract test (if the project has one):
      - Seed the test database with zero rows in the GlamUp table.
      - Call GET /api/glamup.
      - Assert 404 + JSON body.
      - Optionally assert that no 500 is logged.
   c. Regression test: ensure the existing 200 path test still passes when the table has at least one row.

4. CODE REVIEW CHECKLIST (for the Reviewer)
   - [ ] The empty-check is placed before any code that could throw on an empty result.
   - [ ] The 404 JSON body matches the project's standard error envelope.
   - [ ] No new unhandled promise rejections or try/catch gaps introduced.
   - [ ] Rate-limit / standard headers are still present on the 404 response (per postmortem-lessons.md).
   - [ ] All three test cases (empty-table 404, non-empty 200, regression) pass in CI.
   - [ ] No breaking change to the 200 response shape (api-design-guidelines.md deprecation policy).

5. DEFINITION OF DONE
   - Fix merged to main branch.
   - CI pipeline green (lint + all tests).
   - At least one peer approval on the pull request.
   - Behaviour documented in the endpoint's API reference (even a one-line note: 'Returns 404 when no records exist').
